written.q: Define software architecture and software process and explain how they differ.
written.a: Architecture: the high-level structure of a software system, its fundamental components, their interactions and the principles guiding design and evolution; a blueprint addressing performance, scalability, security and maintainability. Process: a structured set of activities, methods and practices to develop and maintain software (requirements, design, coding, testing, deployment, maintenance). Architecture is about what the system is and how it is constructed; process is about how it is developed, managed and delivered. They are distinct but complementary.

written.q: Distinguish digitization, digitalization, digital transformation, AI transformation and human-AI transformation.
written.a: Digitization transforms information (analog to digital); digitalization transforms processes; digital transformation transforms organisations; AI transformation transforms decision-making; human-AI transformation transforms how people create value.

written.q: List the sections of the reverse-engineering presentation and give two non-functional requirements for WhatsApp with reasons.
written.a: Overview, stakeholders, functional requirements, non-functional requirements, high-level architecture, data flow, scalability, security, technology stack. Examples: availability (people expect messages to be delivered at any time) and privacy/security (messages are personal, so encryption and authentication matter).
